integrity.summary: A single request to the product's own CDN was made while auditing the supplied campaign imagery. No remote asset was retained: every image the page renders is served from the repository.
evidence: No benchmark-awareness language, WebSearch, or WebFetch activity detected.
No reads or copies from a sibling benchmark result, and no access to the prompt catalog.
Workflow: 39 file changes, 44 build/test/browser verification actions.
Network access limited to task-required hosts: saveit.mlvcdn.com.

overall.summary: Cleanly built and the best-verified landing page of the pair, but the art direction dims the supplied campaign image almost out of existence, which works against the brief's central instruction.

standards.summary: 3,173 lines across 23 files with the strongest accessibility footprint of the two and 44 verification actions behind it.

findings.title: ask-demo.tsx is 451 lines
findings.detail: The interactive retrieval demo carries state, animation timing and presentation in one file. Splitting the timeline driver from the presentation would make the animation independently adjustable.

strengths: 82 ARIA attributes, the highest of any app in this matrix
All imagery local; the CDN host appears only in the transcript, never in the source

specification.summary: Every required section is present and the copy rules are respected, but the brief's instruction to audit the six supplied images and use them purposefully is only partly honoured in the hero.

findings.title: Hero campaign image is dimmed to near-invisibility
findings.detail: The brief calls for a premium campaign-style use of the supplied imagery. The hero renders the image at very low luminance behind a full-bleed scrim, so the mountain and portal are barely discernible and the section reads as a plain dark gradient. Raise the image's presence or crop into it rather than veiling it.

strengths: Hero, agentic workflow, 100% promise, iOS, pricing, FAQ, closing CTA and footer all present
No em dashes and no invented statistics or testimonials
Free-to-start reassurance under the primary CTA

ux.summary: The centred hero is well balanced and the type is beautifully set, but the composition is conventional where the brief asked for cinematic, and the darkened backdrop costs the page its energy.

findings.title: Centred hero is the safe layout
findings.detail: Kicker, display type, headline, paragraph and two CTAs stacked centrally is the default marketing arrangement. The brief asks for editorial and confident art direction; an asymmetric or overlapping treatment would carry more of that.

strengths: Display serif set at genuine hero scale with restrained tracking
Two-tone headline treatment carries the brand gradient without shouting
Generous vertical rhythm keeps the first screen calm
Responsive down to mobile widths without overflow
